title: Value a nominal forecast in constant dollars

blocks.text: An electricity regulator (invented for this practice) asks every utility to report present values in constant dollars of a base year: amounts deflated to base-year prices and discounted at a real rate. The utility's own forecasts are nominal (each amount in the prices of the year it is paid), and its finance team works with a nominal discount rate. General inflation is `inflation` a year.

Write `constant_dollar_value(forecast, nominal_rate, inflation, base_year)`. `forecast` is `{calendar year: nominal amount}` in $k, paid at the start of each year, and the value is on the start of `base_year`. Your answer must agree with the finance team's nominal value of the same forecast; the regulator only wants it reached in constant dollars.
Write two formulas first: an amount in base-year dollars, and the real rate that matches the nominal one. About six lines.

from __future__ import annotations


def constant_dollar_value(forecast: dict[int, float], nominal_rate: float, inflation: float,
                          base_year: int) -> float:
    """Value on base_year of a nominal forecast, computed in base-year dollars at the real rate."""
    real = (1 + nominal_rate) / (1 + inflation) - 1
    total = 0.0
    for year, amount in forecast.items():
        in_base_dollars = amount / (1 + inflation) ** (year - base_year)
        total += in_base_dollars / (1 + real) ** (year - base_year)
    return total


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(constant_dollar_value({2026: -1000, 2027: 300, 2028: 300, 2029: 300, 2030: 300}, 0.08, 0.03, 2026))

cases.says: with zero inflation, the value is the forecast discounted at the nominal rate
nominal amounts are turned into base-year dollars before the real rate is applied
deflated amounts are discounted at the real rate, not again at the nominal rate
over a long forecast the value matches the nominal-at-nominal value to a billionth, which the approximate real rate does not
